name: Royal Capetian Fortresses of Languedoc
description: Eight hilltop fortresses across Languedoc in southern France, including the walled city of Carcassonne and cliff-top strongholds such as Peyrepertuse, Montségur and Quéribus. Often called "Cathar castles", they were built or reinforced by the French Crown in the 13th and 14th centuries after the Albigensian Crusade. Perched on jagged ridges, they once guarded the new royal frontier.
